A retrospective…

I played Andromeda when it was first released and was “ok” with the game. I missed the old characters and didn’t really embrace the Ryder clan.

Now, years later, I’ve played it again.

While it doesn’t reach the heights of ME2, in some ways there’s a better game under there. There are parts of the story I missed in my first “rush” through the game. I certainly didn’t explore all the side stories.

It’s a much better game than I first thought.

Where I feel there was room for improvement would have been in raising some of the side missions to critical - hello fulcrum. There are stories players can miss as they appear insignificant.

I played this game years ago when i had a bad PC and barely completed the whole story. Now I have a new one and im going through every single side/main quest. Its an amazing game, it has its own little flaws but the community has fixed them through mods. I wish we get another Mass Effect soon.

Mass Effect: Andromeda ends up being a far more engaging experience than its early reputation suggests, especially when you come in expecting a narrative and gameplay mess. The main story delivers a surprisingly compelling arc about exploration, adaptation, and building a new home, and the squad dynamics—while not as iconic as the original trilogy—grow into something genuinely enjoyable, especially Drax. Gameplay is where the game most clearly exceeds expectations: the mobility, combat flow, and class flexibility feel fresh and often exhilarating, making encounters more dynamic than anything in prior Mass Effect titles. That said, the game still carries some classic BioWare shortcuts, especially in side quests that resolve complex dilemmas with overly convenient solutions, and the open world is padded with more fetch‑quest filler than anyone asked for. Even so, the core narrative and moment‑to‑moment gameplay shine enough that, taken on its own terms rather than through the lens of old backlash, Andromeda becomes an unexpectedly rewarding journey.

It's not as good as Mass Effect: Legendary Edition, but few games are. I like the scope of this game; the story is pretty good. Unfortunately, it will (probably) never get the sequel that it leaves itself open for. If you like these kinds of games, it's definitely worth a purchase (especially on sale).
Not as good as ME2&3 but its alright. Ending felt rushed :/ Graphics is insane though
